reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) describes Ti/Ni coatings on diamond particles in an HEA matrix, not Ni additions to W–Cu. It does not address W–Cu wetting, void reduction, or thermal/mechanical properties of W–Cu composites. The key premises about Ni melting, wetting, and property enhancement in W–Cu are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Ni melts and forms a liquid phase at W/Cu interfaces during sintering above 950 °C
The Ni-rich liquid improves wetting and interfacial contact between W and Cu
Improved wetting reduces void formation and phase separation
Reduced voids and better contact enhance thermal transport and mechanical durability
The mechanism is analogous to Ti/Ni coatings improving bonding in diamond/HEA composites
